items.title: Ask HN: How to visually edit vibe coded websites?
items.summary: I like building small sites (plain HTML/CSS/JS) for friends for their small businesses with Claude. It's easy and rewarding. Then I host them on Cloudflare or Netlify with a custom domain, basically free. But then my friends want to update the text and swap pictures. They don't know GitHub or using ChatGpt with Github. Wix and Squarespace feel like overkill, and overpriced, for a few small edits a year. I couldn't find a solution I liked, so I built a proof of concept that edits the Website content visually and pushes the changes back to GitHub. My friends liked it. Now I'm trying to make it usable for more people (https://editany.page/, currently a waitlist only), so I'm definitely biased. I am open to scrap this and join an open source imitative. I just could not find anything easy to use. And I don't want complicated react builds, or a markdown to static website pipeline. I'd like to hear how you handle this. Background: I know to build complex React web apps. But for most small sites, plain HTML/CSS/JS is just enough, plus an external form.

items.title: Show HN: Agency – give your agents the computer you own
items.summary: Everyone is buying a Mac Mini for their agents, or better, giving them a Linux box (see https://x.com/theo/status/2090528543746965991 ). I found this quite tedious to setup every time, so I built a "custom" nixOS image to create a repeatable and customizable computer for my agents. It takes ~5 minutes to install, has a sleek-ish dashboard, and is fully open-source. You could set this up yourself, but for setting up agent multiplexers like T3 Code I find this pretty easy / nice. Show HN: PongArena – Play Pong and see how tiny neural networks think
items.summary: A playground and experiment exploring "how small can a neural network be and still meaningfully play Pong?" You can play against the models directly in your browser, also on mobile, no signup needed. Recommend hitting the fullscreen button for better gameplay. The discussion https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50341174 sparked my interest and I started experimenting a bit with generating neural network weights. I used Codex to program the weights, developing formulas that generate them and refining them using feedback from simulated matches. I also tried one-shot prompting Astra for the weights directly. The surprise, I think, is how hard it’s been in my training attempts to outperform the programmed model using the same 163-parameter architecture. The playground also has some explainers to help interpret the weights, starting from a one-hidden-neuron example with just 13 parameters... It’s all open source, and there is also a league where community weights can be submitted. It would be interesting to see how others would approach this. Can anyone train, prompt or program weights that outperform the initial ones? Code: https://github.com/jonaslindblom/pongarena
